accuracy.reason: All eight card objectives are correct for the explicitly described reverse proxy. Sources support routing policy, sampled health including fail-open behavior, shared state, draining and atomic retry boundaries. Both diagrams preserve selection versus already accepted work.

evidence.quote: Some balancers send traffic to unhealthy targets when every target fails its checks, rather than refusing all traffic.

mechanisms.reason: The cards trace both request directions, connection versus request selection, state loss, delayed failure detection, bounded draining and atomic retry storage. The learner applies those operations to ticketing with supporting quotes.

evidence.quote: Stopping new L4 connections does not stop new HTTP requests on existing connections.

coherence.reason: The Notes example and declared HTTP/database prerequisites support each card. Selection precedes health, routing unit precedes draining, and state scope prepares the shared retry record; capacity closes the same serving path.

evidence.quote: Many note requests can reuse that connection.

decisions.reason: Policy choice is conditional on unequal work and capacity, and omission is allowed for one adequate server. Affinity/shared-state costs, drain interruption, retry load and entry/backend headroom constrain availability decisions.

evidence.quote: Otherwise redirecting traffic can overload them.

clarity.reason: Terms are defined when used and consequences are concrete. Diagrams clearly avoid moving unfinished work between backends; prose explains the limitations of counts, probes, affinity and retries without requiring hidden infrastructure knowledge.

evidence.quote: Session state is information kept between a user's requests.

outcomes.reason: Traces proxy request and response, selects HTTP-aware L7 with decryption, explains connection-pinned L4 requests and allows omission when an adequate server needs neither distribution nor redundant serving.

Explains each policy signal and limitation, conditionally favors weights for measured capacity and connection counts for uneven durations, rejects extra API capacity as a database fix, and requires tested alternate entry plus surviving headroom.

Distinguishes a responding endpoint from usable database-dependent service, covers intervals/coverage/post-check failure, limits removal to new selections and denies automatic completion, undo or safe replay of underway work. Also notes fail-open exceptions.

Explains inaccessible A-only state from B and loss when A fails. Affinity helps placement but neither copies nor saves state; shared storage enables both backends at access/coordination cost and shared availability risk.

Orders cutoff before bounded completion and shutdown, distinguishes accepted work, admits deadline interruption, explains more HTTP work on existing L4 connections and addresses actual connection lifetimes or request acceptance.

Preserves unknown committed outcome and duplicate risk; reuses a stable key across durable shared records, atomically coordinates uniqueness/result/effect, rejects new keys and A-only memory, and bounds delayed retries to avoid overload without claiming success.

sourceChecks.claim: AWS describes distributing incoming traffic across targets, health monitoring and TLS offload. The lesson explicitly limits the shown bidirectional path to a reverse-proxy example and does not require a balancer for one adequate server.
Azure distinguishes transport L4 from HTTP-aware L7, including path routing and TLS offload. The reused-connection consequence and separate backend encryption correctly follow that routing boundary.

NGINX defines round robin, least connections and weighted shares, including varying request duration and combining weights with other policies. The lesson correctly treats these signals as imperfect workload estimates.

AWS health-check documentation confirms periodic intervals, failure thresholds and all-unhealthy fail-open routing. The lesson preserves sample limitations and does not claim checks rescue existing work.

Microsoft web-farm guidance explains that per-node state requires shared storage for cross-node use. NGINX session persistence and AWS target attributes support affinity routing; routing alone does not replicate process memory.

AWS deregistration-delay guidance stops new requests and waits for in-flight work, with early connection termination causing errors. The lesson correctly distinguishes this request-aware example from merely stopping new L4 connections.

AWS idempotent-API guidance supports stable operation identifiers, stored equivalent results and ACID coordination of token and mutation. Shared durable uniqueness closes the cross-backend retry gap; a key alone does not.

Google SRE explains that balancing cannot prevent all overload, request counts hide different resource costs, and load must fit serving capacity or be degraded/rejected. Reachable alternate entry and downstream capacity remain explicit design requirements.
